//: Stylelint for loopy's styles: src/loopy.css, src/print.css and every page's <style> block (tools/lint/check.mjs runs it; CI too). The Baseline rule keeps the CSS to what every browser has had for 30 months (Baseline widely available, data from web-features), so a child's Safari never meets a property it does not know. The ignored properties are safe fall-throughs, each checked: user-select is always written with its -webkit- twin, accent-color and resize fall back to the browser's own look, text-wrap: pretty and balance to normal wrapping, ui-monospace to the next font in the list, and zoom (the card grows on a laptop) has been in every browser since Firefox 126 (May 2024) and falls back to size 1. loopy/no-hard-colour (tools/lint/no-hard-colour.mjs) fails a page on a written-out colour outside src/loopy.css: the themes live in loopy.css, a page takes var(--ink), var(--good) and the rest; the exceptions (custom properties, var() fallbacks, print, SVG pictures, translucent black or white) are listed in that file, and a picture such as a bank note sits between stylelint-disable and stylelint-enable comments that say why.
